Diary, Wednesday
Mrs Pillai called me in first, alone. I expected a lecture. Instead she asked three things: what actually happened with the launch, how it affected me, and what I need now. I said Ojas never sends specs on time. She said, "That's a view of Ojas. What happened, with dates?" So I listed dates. Annoyingly, it helped.
Then she saw Ojas alone. Then both of us, at four.
In the room she kept pulling us back. When I said "He's careless", she said, "Let's stay with the spec problem." When Ojas said "Chaitanya's aggressive", same thing.
By five we'd found the real gap: nobody owns the spec sign-off. I actually listened to him. Weird day.
Chaitanya

One month since Zainab and I sat with our manager and wrote everything down. Today we did our check-in, in the small meeting room, twenty minutes.
What we agreed then: I own client research, she owns the proposals, both names go on every deck, and if something bugs either of us, we say it within a day, privately.

Jyoti was sitting in the common room after lunch, ready to go out, when her friend Mitali messaged to cancel their plan to see the craft fair. Rule one: if a message feels off, ask "what did you mean?" before replying. Rule two: if it still feels off, call. Rule three: if I'm hurt, I wait ten minutes before typing anything.
